back: The growing integration of economies through flows of goods, services, capital, technology, information and people across borders.
Technology and communications, lower transport costs, trade liberalisation, capital mobility (and MNCs).
Relocating production or services to another country, usually to cut costs.
Consumers (lower prices), export industries, skilled workers and countries with good institutions.
Low-skilled workers in industries facing import competition or offshoring, and countries dependent on a few raw materials.
More transport and output raise emissions; technology transfer and higher incomes may help protection.

front: Why can globalisation raise inequality within a country?
back: Gains go mainly to skilled, urban and export-oriented workers and owners.

front: How can a country limit the risks of globalisation?
back: Diversify exports, invest in skills and infrastructure, strengthen institutions and support displaced workers.
